$comment: Regulatory source-of-truth ledger. Every statutory/guideline constant in the codebase has an entry: where it comes from, where it lives in code, when a human last verified it against the official source, and how often it must be re-verified. scripts/regulatory-freshness.cjs (run by npm run checkup and the daily guardian) FAILS when any entry is overdue. When you verify a value against its source, update lastVerified (YYYY-MM-DD). Never change a value without a citation — that is a Correction to the scenario registry.

entries.rule: Deferred/$0-payment student loans qualified at 1% of outstanding balance
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-6-05 (Monthly Debt Obligations)
entries.notes: NC-01 open in the scenarios registry: generated sources claim 0.5% (that is the FHA Handbook 4000.1 figure). Documented IDR payments may be usable per guide — confirm on next verification.

entries.rule: Self-employment/contract income seasoning: 24 months full; 12-24 conditional
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-3.2 (Self-Employment Income)

entries.rule: Single deposits > 50% of monthly qualifying income must be sourced
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-4.2-02 (Depository Accounts); gifts resolved per B3-4.3-04

entries.rule: VA residual income baselines by region/family size; $0.14/sqft utilities; 120% cushion when DTI > 41%
entries.citation: VA Pamphlet 26-7 Chapter 4 (Credit Underwriting), Table 4-2
entries.notes: Residual tables are loan-amount-banded; implemented band is >= $80,000. Verify table values on each review.

entries.rule: Standard DTI ceiling used for flags/what-if coaching
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY referencing legacy QM 43% (12 CFR §1026.43 Appendix Q, repealed 2021 — replaced by price-based General QM)
entries.notes: REVIEW CANDIDATE: DU approves DTIs up to 50% with compensating factors; the 43% figure is a conservative platform flag threshold, not a current federal cap. Decide whether to align flag threshold with DU 50% or keep conservative.

entries.rule: PMI-removal opportunity alert at 80% LTV
entries.citation: Homeowners Protection Act, 12 U.S.C. §4901 et seq. (borrower-requested cancellation at 80% LTV of original value; automatic termination at 78%)
entries.notes: Alert uses current estimated value (AVM); statutory cancellation right keys off original value — the alert is an opportunity signal, the letter/request path must use HPA terms.

entries.rule: Low-reserves warning threshold (months of PITI post-closing)
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY; Fannie reserve requirements (B3-4.1-01) vary by transaction — formal mapping pending
entries.notes: Foundation scenario note in the registry: research proper per-transaction reserve requirements.

entries.rule: Document freshness window used for aging alerts
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY (stricter than Fannie B1-1-03, which allows credit documents up to 4 months old for most transactions)
entries.notes: Deliberately conservative; being stricter than the guideline is compliant. Review whether 30-day nagging is too aggressive once real borrowers exist.

entries.rule: Anti-steering loan-options disclosure before rate lock
entries.citation: Regulation Z, 12 CFR §1026.36(e)(3)
entries.notes: Template text is a summary; legal review recommended before real borrowers sign it (roadmap #26).

entries.rule: FCRA credit-pull disclosure text/version
entries.citation: FCRA §604 (15 U.S.C. §1681b) written-instruction consent

entries.rule: DU submission payload shape
entries.citation: Fannie Mae DU Version 12.1 release notes
entries.notes: Simulated until FANNIE_DU_API_KEY; verify current DU version before go-live.

entries.rule: MISMO export reference model
entries.citation: MISMO v3.4 / Fannie-Freddie ULDD Phase 5 (effective 2025-07-28)

entries.rule: NO federal ban on medical debt in credit reports or underwriting — the CFPB Reg V medical-debt rule was VACATED; do not re-import it
entries.citation: Cornerstone Credit Union League v. CFPB (E.D. Tex., joint request), vacating 'Prohibition on Creditors and CRAs Concerning Medical Information (Regulation V)'; no appeal filed within the window. Same ruling held FCRA preempts state medical-debt reporting bans, so state bans are legally doubtful.
entries.codeRef: CTO_ROADMAP.md #28 (no engine change — documented so nobody encodes the vacated rule)
entries.notes: Bureau voluntary policies still hold: unpaid medical collections < $500 and all paid medical collections are not reported by Equifax/Experian/TransUnion. The pre-production doctrine's 'Medical Debt DTI exclusion (2026 rule)' claim is FALSE as a federal rule; the real, citable medical carve-outs are agency underwriting policies (see fnma-b3-5.3-09-medical-collections and fha-4000-1-collections-capacity).

entries.rule: GSE payoff policy: medical collection accounts excluded from collection/charge-off payoff limits (never required to be paid at/prior to closing); non-medical limits: 1-unit primary none, 2-4-unit owner-occ + second homes > $5,000 total, investment $250 individual / $1,000 total
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-5.3-09 (DU Credit Report Analysis — Past-Due, Collection and Charge-Off of Non-Mortgage Accounts)
entries.codeRef: CTO_ROADMAP.md #28 (not yet in code — activates with F3 real credit adapter; collections do not exist in the simulated soft pull)
entries.notes: Verified against the live guide page 2026-07-04 (guide edition 06/03/2026). The $5,000 2-4-unit/second-home threshold differs from the older $250/$1,000 rule of thumb — re-confirm the exact threshold table on next verification. Freddie Mac equivalent (Guide 5401.2) not yet verified — do so before building the F3 adapter.

entries.rule: FHA capacity analysis: if aggregate NON-MEDICAL collection balances > $2,000, include 5% of outstanding balance as monthly debt in DTI (or documented payment plan, or payoff); MEDICAL collections excluded entirely from the threshold and the DTI add
entries.citation: HUD Handbook 4000.1, Origination through Post-Closing — Collection Accounts (TOTAL: II.A.4.b.iv; Manual: II.A.5.a.iv)
entries.codeRef: CTO_ROADMAP.md #28 (not yet in code — the engine has no collections-to-DTI path today; must ship WITH the F3 adapter or FHA files will compute DTI wrong in both directions)
entries.notes: Subsection letters within II.A.4.b.iv / II.A.5.a.iv shift between handbook updates - cite the Collection Accounts heading, and pin exact subsections when implementing.

entries.rule: Reg B amended effective 2026-07-21: disparate-impact ('effects test') liability removed from Regulation B; 'discouragement' narrowed to intentional statements; SPCP restrictions added
entries.citation: CFPB final rule, Equal Credit Opportunity Act (Regulation B), 91 FR (2026-04-22), docket 2026-07804
entries.notes: Our four-fifths-rule monitoring in fairLendingAnalysis.ts is RETAINED deliberately as internal risk management: HMDA is unaffected, state fair-lending laws still recognize effects-based claims, and the deterministic-decisioning invariants don't depend on Reg B's effects test. Do not delete the monitoring in response to this rule; revisit framing/copy that cites Reg B disparate-impact as a legal requirement. This is the real 'July 2026 Reg B rule' the pre-production doctrine referenced - it is unrelated to medical debt.

entries.rule: Mortgage trigger leads: CRAs may not furnish prescreened consumer reports on residential-mortgage credit inquiries EXCEPT to (a) a party with the consumer's documented opt-in authorization, (b) the originator of the consumer's current mortgage, (c) its current servicer, or (d) an insured depository/credit union holding a current account for the consumer. We must never purchase trigger leads outside these exceptions.
entries.citation: Homebuyers Privacy Protection Act, Pub. L. 119-36 (H.R. 2808, 119th Cong.), signed 2025-09-05, amending FCRA §604(c) (15 U.S.C. §1681b(c)); effective 180 days after enactment
entries.codeRef: server/routes/leads.ts (first-party intake only: TrustedForm cert + consent IP/UA/timestamp evidence; the platform purchases no leads)
entries.notes: Sources split on 2026-03-04 vs 03-05 as the exact effective day (180-day count from 2025-09-05) - immaterial, months past either way. Compliance posture is structural: all lead acquisition is first-party/organic, so HPPA binds us only if we ever start buying leads - re-check this entry before any paid-lead initiative. GAO report on text-based trigger-lead solicitations due 2026-09.

entries.rule: Maximum allowable DTI for DU-underwritten conventional loans
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-6-02 (Debt-to-Income Ratios): 'For loan casefiles underwritten through DU, the maximum allowable DTI ratio is 50%.' Manual underwriting max is 36%, extendable to 45% with Eligibility Matrix credit/reserve requirements.
entries.codeRef: server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts CONVENTIONAL_STRETCH_DTI (DB policy scalar read by server/underwritingEngine.ts)
entries.notes: Verified against the live Selling Guide page 2026-07-04. Our scalar equals the DU ceiling exactly; any value change routes through the guardian/scenario lane.

entries.rule: Baseline DTI ceiling for standard conventional approvals (below-stretch lane)
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY - deliberately conservative baseline. Not an agency figure: Selling Guide B3-6-02 (verified 2026-07-04) allows 50% via DU and 36/45% manual; the pre-2021 ATR/QM 43% appendix-Q threshold this echoes was replaced by the price-based General QM rule.
entries.codeRef: server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts CONVENTIONAL_DTI_CAP (DB policy scalar read by server/underwritingEngine.ts)
entries.notes: Conservative-only overlay: files between 43 and 50 DTI route to the stretch/compensating-factors lane rather than auto-pass, which can never approve something the guide would deny. Relaxing it is a business decision via the guardian/scenario lane.

entries.rule: Minimum representative credit score for conventional conforming eligibility
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-5.1-01 (General Requirements, Credit Scores): minimum 620 for fixed-rate loans, 640 for ARMs, manually underwritten; DU casefiles have no fixed floor (DU assesses risk factors).
entries.codeRef: server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts CONVENTIONAL_FICO_FLOOR (DB policy scalar read by server/underwritingEngine.ts)
entries.notes: Verified against the live Selling Guide page 2026-07-04. Platform applies 620 across the board: exact match for fixed-rate; conservative for DU casefiles (which have no published floor). If ARM products are ever offered, the floor for ARMs is 640 - revisit then.

entries.rule: Maximum LTV for conventional conforming loans
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY - conservative overlay. Selling Guide B2-1.2-01 (verified 2026-07-04) defers numeric LTV maximums to the Eligibility Matrix; standard 1-unit principal-residence max is 95%, with 95.01-97% available only under specific programs the platform deliberately does not offer yet.
entries.codeRef: server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts CONVENTIONAL_LTV_CAP (DB policy scalar read by server/underwritingEngine.ts)
entries.notes: Eligibility Matrix PDF is bot-protected (HTTP 403 on 2026-07-04) - the 95/97 split needs a HUMAN verification pass against the downloaded matrix; B2-1.2-01 page itself was fetched and confirms the matrix is the numeric authority. Offering 97% LTV products later is a business decision via the guardian/scenario lane.

entries.rule: Valuation haircut applied to stock/investment assets in pre-underwriting capacity checks
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY - strictly-conservative overlay. VERIFIED AGENCY BASELINE (B3-4.3-01, fetched 2026-07-04): Fannie requires NO percentage haircut - most-recent-statement value is used, and for reserves '100% of the value of the assets may be considered'.
entries.codeRef: server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts HAIRCUT_STOCK_INVESTMENT (DB policy scalar read by server/underwritingEngine.ts)
entries.notes: Counting only 60% of the asset is stricter than the guide, so it can never approve a file the guide would deny - it CAN under-state buying power. Revisit with F3/F4 real asset verification: market-volatility haircuts are a legitimate platform risk choice but should be an explicit product decision, not an assumed agency rule.

entries.rule: Valuation haircut applied to retirement assets in pre-underwriting capacity checks
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY - conservative overlay approximating access costs (penalties/taxes) on retirement funds. Formal mapping to Selling Guide B3-4.3-03 (retirement accounts) pending human verification.
entries.codeRef: server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts HAIRCUT_RETIREMENT (DB policy scalar read by server/underwritingEngine.ts)
entries.notes: Same conservative-only property as platform-haircut-stock-60. Verify B3-4.3-03's current documentation/accessibility conditions on the next pass and decide whether the 70% overlay stays as product policy.

entries.rule: FHFA conforming loan limit, one-unit baseline (loans above route to jumbo)
entries.citation: FHFA 2026 conforming loan limit values, one-unit baseline (contiguous US). Documented inline in shared/lendingLimits.ts as the FHFA 2026 figure.
entries.codeRef: shared/lendingLimits.ts CONFORMING_LOAN_LIMIT_2026; server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts CONFORMING_LOAN_LIMIT scalar; jumbo boundary BRC-J30 (min 806500.01)
entries.notes: FHFA publishes new limits each November for the following year - the 2027 update is a seed + BRC-J30 boundary change, and prod/dev reseeds must move together (seedMarketPricing is skip-if-exists).

entries.rule: Window for flagging recently opened tradelines as sleeper debt in liability adjustment
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY - conservative detection window. Selling Guide B3-6-05 requires ALL monthly debts including recently opened accounts in the DTI; it does not publish a fixed recency window. The 90-day flag window is the platform's own sleeper-debt detection heuristic (roadmap #32 resolution, 2026-07-04).
entries.notes: The flagged lines' payments are already included in adjustedMonthlyDebt either way - the window only controls the newTradelines advisory surface, so it is detection metadata, not a qualification rule. Same pattern as platform-reserves-2-months.
